Class VirtualServerTCP

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.client.virtualserver.VirtualServerTCP
All Implemented Interfaces:
VirtualServer, AutoCloseable, Runnable
public class VirtualServerTCP extends Object implements VirtualServer, Runnable
TCP implementation of the VirtualServer role.

In the client architecture, ServerProxyTCP and VirtualServerTCP share the same TCP socket but own opposite communication directions:

  • ServerProxyTCP writes client-to-server commands, such as authentication or lobby actions;
  • VirtualServerTCP reads server-to-client messages, such as errors, lobby updates, game updates, and heartbeat pings.

This class is started by ServerProxyTCP in a dedicated background thread. Its job is to continuously read one JSON message per line from the socket, rebuild the corresponding ServerMessage, and forward it to the client view through MessageRouter.

It does not contain UI logic and it does not contain game logic. The UI-specific rendering belongs to ClientView; the game rules belong to the server. This class is only the TCP receiver and dispatcher for messages that the server sends to this client.

Connection shutdown has one important rule: if the client intentionally closes the connection, the receiver must stop silently; if the connection ends without a client-side close request, the receiver reports a CONNECTION_CLOSED error to the view.

  • Constructor Details

    • VirtualServerTCP

      public VirtualServerTCP(Socket socket, ClientView clientView, ServerProxyTCP serverProxy)
      Creates the TCP receiver for one client connection.

      The socket is the same socket used by ServerProxyTCP. This object reads from the socket input stream, while the proxy writes to the socket output stream. The serverProxy reference is needed for two lifecycle operations: sending a PONG when the server sends PING, and closing the shared connection when the receiver stops.

      Parameters:
      socket - connected TCP socket shared with ServerProxyTCP
      clientView - client-side view contract used by MessageRouter
      serverProxy - matching TCP proxy used to send PONG messages and close the connection

  • Method Details

    • requestCloseByClient

      public void requestCloseByClient()
      Marks that the next socket closure is expected because it was requested by the client.

      This method is called by ServerProxyTCP.close() before closing the socket. Without this flag, the receiver would interpret the end of the input stream as an unexpected server-side disconnection and would show a CONNECTION_CLOSED error to the user.

    • run

      public void run()
      Runs the TCP receiving loop.

      The loop blocks on the socket input stream and reads server messages line by line. Each line is expected to contain one serialized JSON ServerMessage. When the input stream ends, this method decides whether the closure is normal or unexpected by checking requestCloseByClient() state.

      If the connection ends unexpectedly, the method routes a CONNECTION_CLOSED error to the view. If the client requested the close, no user-facing error is produced.

      The finally block closes the shared TCP connection through ServerProxyTCP.closeConnection() so that both directions of the socket are released when the receiver stops.

      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable

    • handleMessage

      public void handleMessage(ServerMessage message)
      Routes one typed server message to the client view layer.

      The routing decision is delegated to MessageRouter, so this class remains focused on networking and protocol conversion.

      Specified by:

      Parameters:

    • handlePing

      public void handlePing()
      Handles the TCP heartbeat request sent by the server.

      PING is not shown to the user. The receiver answers by asking ServerProxyTCP to send a PONG on the client-to-server direction of the same connection.

      Specified by:
      handlePing in interface VirtualServer

    • close

      public void close() throws IOException
      Closes the shared TCP connection through the matching ServerProxyTCP.

      The actual socket is owned together with the proxy, so this method delegates to the proxy connection closing primitive instead of closing only the receiver input path.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Specified by:
      close in interface VirtualServer
